_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 3 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 2 Flowering Plants. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in order (roots and stem; leaves and flower; warm or cold; a fair test; a conclusion, here as the lesson's own record table and then the conclusion), in the lesson's own words: its tap figure (ART.figure 'plant', one part named at a time), its warm-and-cold test (ART.pots with coldB, the plantWarm sim's own options) and its record step, two rows and the lesson's own choices.
title: Flowering Plants
subtitle: Grade 3 Science
objectives: Describe the function of the major parts of flowering plants (limited to roots, leaves, stems and flowers).
Know that plants need appropriate conditions, including temperature, light and water, to be healthy.
Make a prediction describing some possible outcomes of an enquiry.
Collect and record observations and/or measurements in tables and diagrams.
Identify whether results support, or do not support, a prediction.
Make a conclusion from results and relate it to the scientific question being investigated.

beats.say: A flowering plant has four main parts. Each part has a job to do.
You will find out what each part does, and what a plant needs.
Here is a whole flowering plant. Let us start under the soil.
These are the roots. They anchor the plant in the soil.
They hold it so well that the wind cannot blow it over.

at.wind: the wind cannot blow it over

beats.say: The roots also take in water and minerals from the soil.
This is the stem. It holds the plant up towards the light.
The stem carries that water to every leaf and flower.
These are the leaves. They are wide and flat, to catch as much light as they can.
They catch sunlight and use it to make the plant's food.
Roots do not eat soil. The food is made in the leaves.
This is the flower. Its bright petals attract insects.
The flower makes seeds, so there can be new plants.
A flower is one part of a plant, not the whole plant.
A plant needs water and light. It also needs the right temperature.
Today you will keep one plant warm and put one somewhere very cold.
Both plants get the same water and the same light.
What will happen to the cold plant after five days?
Say what you think first. What you think is your prediction.
Only one thing changes: the temperature.
The water and the light stay the same. That is a fair test.
Day after day, the warm plant stays healthy and green.
By day five the cold plant has drooped and gone yellow.
Write down what you saw. A table keeps your results tidy.
One row for the warm plant. One row for the cold plant.
Warm plant: healthy and green. Cold plant: drooping and yellow.
Now a scientist asks two questions about the results.
The first is this. Did the results support my prediction?
You predicted the cold plant would droop, and it did.
The second question is what the results tell you. That is a conclusion.
Plants need the right temperature, as well as water and light.
Roots take in water. The stem carries it to the leaves.
Leaves make the food, and the flower makes the seeds.
A plant needs water, light and the right temperature.

at.needs: water, light and the right temperature

beats.say: You predicted, you tested, you wrote it down, and you concluded.
